extraction.Name: Emma Valandry
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want her patent to her allotment of 320 acres, for she did not want to pay the taxes, but that it was sent to her twice, and she finally accepted it
extraction.Buyer: first mortgaged to a man by the name of Beeby for $1000.00; second mortgage for $2000.00; sold in 1926 to a man by the name of Ellis, of White River, South Dakota, for $6400.00, he assuming the second mortgage, paying the deponent $780.00 in cash, and giving his note for the balance; Ellis traded the place to another fellow; deponent traded her notes received from Mr. Ellis for property in Martin, South Dakota
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: in 1919 she was stricken with severe heart trouble, and, to raise money to go to the Mayo Bros., Hospital, Rochester, Minnesota, she mortgaged her allotment; again account of sickness, in 1920, she mortgaged it for $2000.00, was unable to keep up the payments on this second mortgage
extraction.Occupation/Income: income being from rental of town houses, and the salary from her husband's janitor work for the high school
extraction.NOTES: mentally incompetent; health is exceedingly poor; has spent all the money she could obtain for hospital and doctor bills, both in Rochester, Minnesota and in Gordon, Nebraska, being bothered principally with her heart, sometimes having fainting spells; husband supports her and one minor child; has never received any help from the County or Government; affidavit subscribed and sworn to before notary public on November 17, 1928; Shannon County, South Dakota | TASK 3 BULK TRIBE INFERENCE 2026-04-29: Tribe field set to 'Pine Ridge' based on directory provenance (record is filed in pine_ridge_*/extractions/, which corresponds to the NARA RG 75 Pine Ridge Vol 1, Vol 2, and Vol 3 bound volumes of Circular 2464 responses). 67 such records were originally 'not stated'; 6 received BLM-confirmed substantive patches in the same transaction; the remaining 61 (this record's batch) are inferred from directory and geographic/naming evidence. Inference is rebuttable — any record can be re-evaluated via BLM cross-reference if its Pine Ridge affiliation is questioned.
